description: Retrieves the alarms for the specified metric.

parameters.name: access_key
parameters.description: AWS access key ID. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID or AWS_ACCESS_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The aws_access_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_access_key_id alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: action_prefix
parameters.description: This parameter can be used to filter the results of the operation to only those alarms that use a certain alarm action.

parameters.name: alarm_name_prefix
parameters.description: An alarm name prefix to retrieve information about alarms that have names that start with this prefix. Can not be used with alarm_names.

parameters.name: alarm_type
parameters.description: Specify this to return metric alarms or composite alarms. Module is defaulted to return metric alarms but can return composite alarms if alarm_type=CompositeAlarm. Choices: "CompositeAlarm" "MetricAlarm" ← (default)

parameters.name: aws_ca_bundle
parameters.description: The location of a CA Bundle to use when validating SSL certificates. The AWS_CA_BUNDLE environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: aws_config
parameters.description: A dictionary to modify the botocore configuration. Parameters can be found in the AWS documentation https://botocore.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/reference/config.html#botocore.config.Config.

parameters.name: children_of_alarm_name
parameters.description: If specified returns information about the “children” alarms of the alarm name specified.

parameters.name: debug_botocore_endpoint_logs
parameters.description: Use a botocore.endpoint logger to parse the unique (rather than total) "resource:action" API calls made during a task, outputing the set to the resource_actions key in the task results. Use the aws_resource_action callback to output to total list made during a playbook. The ANSIBLE_DEBUG_BOTOCORE_LOGS environment variable may also be used. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: endpoint_url
parameters.description: URL to connect to instead of the default AWS endpoints. While this can be used to connection to other AWS-compatible services the amazon.aws and community.aws collections are only tested against AWS. The AWS_URL environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: parents_of_alarm_name
parameters.description: If specified returns information about the “parent” alarms of the alarm name specified.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: A named AWS profile to use for authentication. See the AWS documentation for more information about named profiles https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-profiles.html. The AWS_PROFILE environment variable may also be used. The profile option is mutually exclusive with the aws_access_key, aws_secret_key and session_token options.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The AWS region to use. For global services such as IAM, Route53 and CloudFront, region is ignored. The AWS_REGION environment variable may also be used. See the Amazon AWS documentation for more information http://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#ec2_region.

parameters.name: secret_key
parameters.description: AWS secret access key. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY or AWS_SECRET_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The secret_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_secret_access_key alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: session_token
parameters.description: AWS STS session token for use with temporary credentials. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SESSION_TOKEN environment variable may also be used. The session_token and profile options are mutually exclusive.

parameters.name: state_value
parameters.description: If specified returns information only about alarms that are currently in the particular state. Choices: "OK" "ALARM" "INSUFFICIENT_DATA"

parameters.name: validate_certs
parameters.description: When set to false, SSL certificates will not be validated for communication with the AWS APIs. Setting validate_certs=false is strongly discouraged, as an alternative, consider setting aws_ca_bundle instead. Choices: false true ← (default)

examples:
# Note: These examples do not set authentication details, see the AWS Guide for details.

- name: describe the metric alarm based on alarm names
  amazon.aws.cloudwatch_metric_alarm_info:
    alarm_names:
      - my-test-alarm-1
      - my-test-alarm-2

- name: describe the metric alarm based alarm names and state value
  amazon.aws.cloudwatch_metric_alarm_info:
    alarm_names:
      - my-test-alarm-1
      - my-test-alarm-2
    state_value: OK

- name: describe the metric alarm based alarm names prefix
  amazon.aws.cloudwatch_metric_alarm_info:
    alarm_name_prefix: my-test-

return_values.name: metric_alarms
return_values.description: The gathered information about specified metric alarms. Returned: when success

return_values.name: actions_enabled
return_values.description: Indicates whether actions should be executed during any changes to the alarm state. Returned: always

return_values.name: alarm_actions
return_values.description: The actions to execute when this alarm transitions to an ALARM state from any other state. Returned: always

return_values.name: alarm_arn
return_values.description: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the alarm. Returned: always

return_values.name: alarm_configuration_updated_timestamp
return_values.description: The time stamp of the last update to the alarm configuration. Returned: always

return_values.name: alarm_description
return_values.description: The description of the alarm. Returned: always

return_values.name: alarm_name
return_values.description: Unique name for the alarm. Returned: always

return_values.name: comparison_operator
return_values.description: The arithmetic operation to use when comparing the specified statistic and threshold. Returned: always

return_values.name: datapoints_to_alarm
return_values.description: The number of data points that must be breaching to trigger the alarm. Returned: always

return_values.name: dimensions
return_values.description: The dimensions for the metric. Returned: always

return_values.name: name
return_values.description: The name of the dimension. Returned: always

return_values.name: value
return_values.description: The value of the dimension. Returned: always

return_values.name: evaluate_low_sample_count_percentile
return_values.description: Used only for alarms based on percentiles. If ignore, the alarm state does not change during periods with too few data points to be statistically significant. If evaluate or this parameter is not used, the alarm is always evaluated and possibly changes state. Returned: always

return_values.name: evaluation_period
return_values.description: The number of periods over which data is compared to the specified threshold. Returned: always

return_values.name: extended_statistic
return_values.description: The percentile statistic for the metric associated with the alarm. Returned: always

return_values.name: insufficient_data_actions
return_values.description: The actions to execute when this alarm transitions to an INSUFFICIENT_DATA state from any other state. Returned: always

return_values.name: metric_name
return_values.description: Name of the monitored metric (e.g. CPUUtilization). Returned: always

return_values.name: metrics
return_values.description: An array of MetricDataQuery structures, used in an alarm based on a metric math expression. Returned: always

return_values.name: namespace
return_values.description: Name of the appropriate namespace (AWS/EC2, System/Linux, etc.). Determines the category it will appear under in CloudWatch. Returned: always

return_values.name: ok_actions
return_values.description: The actions to execute when this alarm transitions to an OK state from any other state. Returned: always

return_values.name: period
return_values.description: The length, in seconds, used each time the metric specified in MetricName is evaluated. Valid values are 10, 30, and any multiple of 60. Returned: always

return_values.name: state_reason
return_values.description: An explanation for the alarm state, in text format. Returned: always

return_values.name: state_reason_data
return_values.description: An explanation for the alarm state, in JSON format. Returned: always

return_values.name: state_updated_timestamp
return_values.description: The time stamp of the last update to the alarm state. Returned: always

return_values.name: state_value
return_values.description: The state value for the alarm. Returned: always

return_values.name: statistic
return_values.description: The statistic for the metric associated with the alarm, other than percentile. Returned: always

return_values.name: threshold
return_values.description: The value to compare with the specified statistic. Returned: always

return_values.name: threshold_metric_id
return_values.description: This is the ID of the ANOMALY_DETECTION_BAND function used as the threshold for the alarm. Returned: always

return_values.name: treat_missing_data
return_values.description: Sets how alarm is to handle missing data points. Returned: always

return_values.name: unit
return_values.description: Unit used when storing the metric Returned: always
